meaning.situation_summary: A neighbour, Femke from number twelve, writes that a hen is walking in your garden eating your tomatoes, asks whether it is yours and says she is home until six.
meaning.communicative_purpose: The reader learns about the hen, can tell Femke whether it is theirs and knows until what time she is at home.
meaning.contrivance_check: A neighbour's note about an animal in the garden is plausible. The humour is one familiar animal in an unusual place; the question 'Is dat uw kip?' is natural for someone who sees the hen. 'U kunt mij bellen' assumes the neighbours know each other's number, which is ordinary.
meaning.image_text_link: A brown hen on a lawn behind a terraced house shows the animal without tomatoes, a time or a person, so it favours neither distractor.

meaning.situation_summary: A shop tells a customer that the new coat is in the shop on Friday, that they can collect it, that the shop is open until six and that it costs forty euro.
meaning.communicative_purpose: The customer knows on which day the coat is in the shop and what to pay.
meaning.contrivance_check: The original 'nu in de winkel' together with 'vrijdag ophalen' contradicted itself and was rewritten. Collecting an ordered coat and paying at the shop is ordinary. The shop name Winkel De Jas is plain and descriptive; two web searches (28 October 2026) found no shop of that name.
meaning.image_text_link: A single coat on a rail in a quiet clothes shop fits the message and shows no price, person, day or time.
